"# Implementation Plan: Enhanced GitHub Landing Page

Enhance the landing page of the application with a premium, high-fidelity experience matching the new roadmap. We will install Swiper.js, GSAP, Lenis smooth scroll, and design a custom, modular structure for the sections.

## User Review Required

> [!IMPORTANT]
> - We will install new dependencies: `gsap`, `swiper`, `lenis`, and `react-intersection-observer`.
> - To avoid naming conflicts with the existing dashboard layout elements (which also use a Navbar and Footer), we will place the new landing page components in `src/components/landing/` (e.g., `src/components/landing/Navbar.jsx`, `src/components/landing/Footer.jsx`, etc.).

## Proposed Changes

We will build the landing page sections as modular React components and integrate them into `src/pages/Landing.jsx`.

### Directory & Component Map

```
src/
├── components/
│   ├── landing/
│   │   ├── Navbar.jsx          # Sticky header with glassmorphism & drop-down menus
│   │   ├── Hero.jsx            # Animated hero text, CTA buttons, and glowing backgrounds
│   │   ├── FeatureTabs.jsx     # Tabs for Code, Plan, Collaborate, Automate, Secure
│   │   ├── FeatureSection.jsx  # Two-column layout showcasing features dynamically
│   │   ├── LogoSection.jsx     # Auto-scrolling logo marquee
│   │   ├── CaseStudies.jsx     # High-end interactive case study hover cards
│   │   ├── IndustryTabs.jsx    # Segmented tabs changing card structures
│   │   ├── CustomerStories.jsx # Grid of testimonials and hover highlights
│   │   ├── CTA.jsx             # Action section with gradients and floating elements
│   │   └── Footer.jsx          # Detailed multi-column footer layout
│   └── ... (existing components)
├── hooks/
│   ├── useScroll.js            # Hook for scroll tracking
│   └── useAnimation.js         # Hook for GSAP intersection reveals

I have found and resolved the issues that were causing the blank screen.

### 🔍 What Caused the Blank Screen?
Because of JSX compilation rules in React, curly braces inside code mockup illustrations (which were meant to be displayed as literal code snippets) were being evaluated by the React compiler at runtime. 
1. **`children` is not defined**: React was attempting to evaluate `{ children }` in `FeatureSection.jsx` as an active variable rather than text.
2. **`toggle` is not defined**: React was trying to evaluate the `{toggle}` expression in the `<Navbar toggle={toggle} />` mockup code line.
3. **`Link` is not defined**: We had used the `<Link>` router component in the Feature Section but the import statement was missing from the top of `FeatureSection.jsx`.

### 🛠️ Resolution & Fixes
- Wrapped all raw code mockups in string blocks (e.g. `{"Button = ({ children }) => ("}`) inside `FeatureSection.jsx` and `Hero.jsx` so the compiler treats them strictly as static text.
- Added the missing `import { Link } from 'react-router-dom'` at the top of `FeatureSection.jsx`.

The Vite compilation has successfully reloaded, and `npm run build` passes cleanly.

"# Walkthrough: Full-Stack Authentication (Firebase Auth + Express + MongoDB)

We have fully built the authentication roadmap. The backend Express API server is active and running on port 5000 in the background, and the frontend Vite/React app has been refactored to use Firebase hooks and Zod form validations.

## 🚀 Key Accomplishments

### 1. Express Backend Setup (`backend/`)
We created a clean Node.js API with Express, Mongoose, and security headers:
- **MongoDB Connection (`backend/config/db.js`)**: Connects to the database (fallback option to in-memory/simulated logs when Atlas URI is not provided).
- **Mongoose Model (`backend/models/User.js`)**: Maps Firebase user UID, provider type, roles (user, contributor, admin), and email verification status.
- **JWT & Cookie Session (`backend/routes/authRoutes.js`)**: Signs a JWT token and returns it in an **HTTP-Only, secure cookie** (`token`) to the browser to prevent XSS-based theft.
- **Route Endpoints**:
  - `POST /api/auth/register`: Syncs a registered client account to MongoDB.
  - `POST /api/auth/login`: Validates the active user session.
  - `POST /api/auth/google`: OAuth popup sync. Creates new records or logs in existing Google accounts.
  - `POST /api/auth/logout`: Clears the HTTP-only JWT token cookie.
  - `GET /api/user/profile`: Private route returning user details from MongoDB.
  - `PUT /api/user/update`: Private route updating names or profile avatar URLs.
- **Security Middlewares (`backend/middleware/`)**:
  - `authMiddleware.js`: Verifies JWT cookie signature and extracts user references.
  - `errorMiddleware.js`: Intercepts errors and returns JSON stack logs.
  - Express main server (`server.js`) utilizes `helmet` headers, CORS configuration with credentials support, and a `express-rate-limit` request rate limiter.

### 2. Frontend Auth Integration
- **Firebase Initialization (`src/services/firebase.js`)**: Registers Firebase Client connection using environment keys (fallbacks to test strings if empty).

### 🔑 Local Testing and Developer Sandbox

To make testing as easy as possible before you plug in your production Firebase keys, the application is pre-configured with a **Developer Sandbox Mode** (which activates automatically when the Firebase keys in `.env` are left blank):

1. **Email / Password Signup & Login**:
   - Go to `/register` and fill out the details (First Name, Last Name, Username, Email, Password). 
   - Notice the **Password Strength Meter** update as you type.
   - Click **Create Account**. It will simulate creating an account, register it with the backend server, and redirect you to `/verify-email`.
   - On the verification screen, click the **"Developer Sandbox: Auto-Verify Email"** button. This bypasses the email validation, tags the account as verified, and redirects you directly to the dashboard!
2. **Google OAuth popup Simulation**:
   - Go to `/login` and click the **"Continue with Google"** button.
   - It will mock the Google popup integration, create a synced user profile on the MongoDB database, and log you in.
3. **Session Persistence**:
   - Refresh the page inside the dashboard. It checks the token credentials and maintains your logged-in state.
   - Click **Sign Out** in the sidebar. It clears cookies and redirects you back to `/login`.

### 📂 File Structure Added:
- **`backend/`**: Node.js/Express server in ES Modules format.
  - `server.js` (main entrypoint, security helmet headers, CORS settings, cookie parser, and request rate limits).
  - `config/db.js` (database connection with error logging).
  - `models/User.js` (user schema: UID, email, name, avatar, verification flag, user roles).
  - `routes/authRoutes.js` (JWT signing, register syncing, Google SSO syncing, logout, profile endpoints).
  - `middleware/` (JWT cookies verification and global error interceptors).
- **`src/` (Frontend Updates)**:
  - `services/firebase.js` (client SDK initialization).
  - `api/axios.js` (instance with `withCredentials` enabled to send cookies).
  - `context/AuthContext.jsx` & `hooks/useAuth.js` (monitors state and triggers OAuth popups or register syncs).

I have found the issue causing the white screen at `/login` and corrected it!

### 🔍 What Caused the Blank Page on Login?
The project previously used a **Redux slice state** (`state.auth`) to manage session credentials, which was pre-initialized to `isAuthenticated: true` so the static dashboard template ran out-of-the-box.

When we integrated the **Firebase + MongoDB backend authentication** flow, we introduced `AuthContext` (React Context) which correctly initialized the logged-in state to `null` on first load. This mismatch created an **infinite redirect loop**:
1. When you visited `/login`, the wrapper `AuthLayout` checked the Redux state, saw `isAuthenticated: true`, and immediately navigated you to `/dashboard`.
2. When the router loaded `/dashboard`, the `ProtectedRoute` checked the context session, saw that the Firebase/Mock user was actually `null` (since you hadn't signed in yet), and redirected you back to `/login`.
3. This loop occurred at lightning speed in the background, causing React to throw a `Maximum update depth exceeded` error and rendering a blank page.

### 🛠️ Resolution & Fixes
1. **Redux State Sync**:
   - Modified `authSlice.js` to initialize `isAuthenticated: false` and `user: null` by default.
   - Refactored `AuthContext.jsx` to declare an `updateUserState` wrapper. Now, whenever the user state changes (like during page refreshes, signups, logins, or logouts), it automatically dispatches the corresponding Redux action (`reduxLogin` or `reduxLogout`) keeping both layers perfectly in sync.
2. **Main Layout Hook Binding**:
   - Updated `MainLayout.jsx`'s sidebar logout button to call the `logout` trigger from `useAuth()` directly rather than firing a isolated Redux action, which ensures that backend JWT cookies and Firebase sessions are correctly cleared on logout.

We will move the authentication layouts and pages into `src/auth/`:

"# Walkthrough: Re-Authentication System & Folder Restructuring

We have successfully implemented the Re-Authentication System and restructured the authentication pages folder.

## 🚀 Key Accomplishments

### 1. Folder Reorganization (`src/auth/`)
We created the `src/auth/` directory and consolidated all authentication views:
- **`src/auth/AuthLayout.jsx`**: Layout container (removed the Redux `isAuthenticated` gate). Now, navigating to `/login` always renders the credentials input boxes, even if a user is logged in.
- **`src/auth/Login.jsx`**: Custom form with Zod schema resolution, validation feedback, and a new **Show/Hide Password** icon toggle.
- **`src/auth/Signup.jsx`** (Renamed/Relocated from `Register.jsx`): Multi-field form (First Name, Last Name, Username, Email, Password, Confirm Password) and a visual **Password Strength indicator**.
- **`src/auth/ForgotPassword.jsx`**: User password recovery router link.
- **`src/auth/GoogleLogin.jsx`** (New component): Reusable OAuth button triggering Firebase Google OAuth popups.

### 2. File Cleanups & Routing Mappings
- **Deletions**: Removed outdated duplicates (`src/layouts/AuthLayout.jsx`, `src/pages/Login.jsx`, `src/pages/Register.jsx`, `src/pages/ForgotPassword.jsx`).
- **`AppRoutes.jsx`**: Updated all import pathways to source the files from the new `../auth/` directory and updated `/register` to point directly to `<Signup />`.

### 3. Session Replacement & Security Logic
- **`AuthContext.jsx`**: Created a `clearSession()` utility. When a user submits credentials for a new account (via email/password or Google SSO), the system destroys any previous `mock_user` records, wipes backend token cookies via `/api/auth/logout`, clears the active context user, and immediately generates a clean authenticated session.
- **`MainLayout.jsx`**: Updated the sidebar sign-out button to trigger the async context `logout()` call, clearing cookies and Firebase sessions rather than only firing local Redux changes.

We have successfully integrated a complete, premium visual effects system to recreate GitHub's high-end landing page aesthetics! We also resolved a hidden profile stats rendering exception.

- **`MouseGlow.jsx`**: An interactive radial gradient overlay that follows the cursor.

- **`Hero.jsx`**: Mockup window wrapped in a premium float animation (`animate-float-premium`).

"# Walkthrough: Visual Design & Animation Systems

We have fully implemented the visual layout configurations outlined in the design roadmap!

## 🚀 Key Accomplishments

### 1. Extended Design System Colors
- **`tailwind.config.js`**: Registered the custom color codes under the `brand` namespace (including `bgPrimary`, `bgSecondary`, `bgCard`, `border`, and glow accents).

### 2. Viewport Scroll Reveals (`src/components/landing/SectionReveal.jsx`)
- Built a reusable wrapper component that listens to screen viewport coordinates. It creates a smooth entrance transition for each content section, shifting from blurred (`filter: blur(6.5px)`) and slightly offset to fully focused as you scroll down.

### 3. Pausable Logo Marquee (`src/components/landing/LogoMarquee.jsx`)
- Replaced the old `LogoSection` with an improved version. The marquee infinitely scrolls horizontally, pauses on hover (`hover:[animation-play-state:paused]`), and fades out on the left and right edges against the `#0D1117` background using clean gradient masks.

### 4. Mascot Vector SVGs & Floating Components
- **`src/components/landing/FloatingObject.jsx`**: Reusable container utilizing Framer Motion keyframes.
- **`src/components/landing/Hero.jsx`**: Created three custom inline SVG mascot vectors:
  - **Futuristic Robot Head**: Floating with a purple drop shadow on the left.
  - **Golden Duck Mascot**: Floating with an orange glow on the bottom-right.
  - **3D Sphere**: Drifts with a pink/purple radial mesh gradient.

---

"# Implementation Plan: Continuous Premium Background System

Refactor the landing page layout to support a single, unified background canvas running from the Hero all the way underneath the Footer. This removes all solid dividers and horizontal page breaks, and enables lighting effects to drift naturally across the page.

## User Review Required

> [!IMPORTANT]
> - We will structure the background canvas into a dedicated modular folder: `src/components/AnimatedBackground/`.
> - The component layers will consist of:
>   1. `GlobalGradient.jsx` (long linear base gradient backdrop)
>   2. `GlowLayer.jsx` (ambient pulsing glows positioned across Hero, Features, CTA, and Footer)
>   3. `ParticleLayer.jsx` (fixed-position GPU-friendly HTML5 canvas dust generator)
>   4. `NoiseLayer.jsx` (fixed grain noise blending SVG overlay)
>   5. `BackgroundAnimation.jsx` (the unified orchestrator)
> - All section elements in `Landing.jsx` and the container classes in `Footer.jsx` and `CTA.jsx` will be configured to be transparent to prevent color blocking.

## Proposed Changes

### File Restructuring Map

```
src/
├── components/
│   ├── AnimatedBackground/
│   │   ├── GlobalGradient.jsx      # [NEW] Multi-stop base linear backdrop
│   │   ├── GlowLayer.jsx           # [NEW] Multi-orb positioning layer
│   │   ├── ParticleLayer.jsx       # [NEW] Fixed canvas particle generator
│   │   ├── NoiseLayer.jsx          # [NEW] Transparent overlay grain
│   │   └── BackgroundAnimation.jsx # [NEW] Unified background component
│   └── landing/
│       ├── Footer.jsx              # [MODIFY] Transparent glass border setup
│       ├── CTA.jsx                 # [MODIFY] Remove canvas backgrounds
│       └── CustomerStories.jsx     # [MODIFY] Remove solid backgrounds
└── styles/
    └── background.css              # [NEW] Background layouts stylesheet
```

"# Walkthrough: Continuous Premium Background System

We have successfully refactored the visual layout to support a single, unified background canvas running continuously from the Hero all the way underneath the Footer!

## 🚀 Key Accomplishments

### 1. Unified Background System (`src/components/AnimatedBackground/`)
Created a dedicated directory for background layers, breaking it down into modular, highly performant sub-components:
- **`GlobalGradient.jsx`**: Renders a vertical linear gradient spanning the entire document height, smoothly transitioning from `#0D1117` to `#161B22` and back without harsh breaks.
- **`GlowLayer.jsx`**: Positions slowly pulsing, heavily blurred HSL glowing orbs dynamically at key sections of the page (Hero, Features, Testimonials, CTA, and Footer).
- **`ParticleLayer.jsx`**: Renders a fixed-position HTML5 canvas particle generator, drawing floating nodes only within the visible screen viewport to ensure optimal performance.
- **`NoiseLayer.jsx`**: Overlays a subtle SVG grain/noise texture fixed to the screen.
- **`BackgroundAnimation.jsx`**: Assembles and wraps all the above layers into a single container.

### 2. Transparent Sections & Footer Integration
Removed all solid backgrounds from landing sections to let the glow animations show through:
- **`Footer.jsx`**: Removed the solid gray background class `bg-github-dark-sidebar/30`. The footer is now transparent and continues the global animated background with a glassmorphic top border (`border-[#30363D]/45`).
- **`CTA.jsx`**: Removed the canvas solid backgrounds, converting it to a transparent block.
- **`CustomerStories.jsx`**: Replaced solid background containers with `bg-transparent`.
- **`Landing.jsx`**: Updated to load `<BackgroundAnimation />` and clean up the legacy duplicate overlays.

### 3. Stylesheet Cleanups
- **`background.css`**: Created to define absolute layout sizes and fixed canvas positions.
- **`index.css`**: Registered the `background.css` stylesheet at the top imports list.

---\

"# Walkthrough: Customer Success Stories Redesign

We have successfully rebuilt the Customer Success Stories (Testimonials) section using a highly modular folder structure inspired by GitHub's enterprise pages.

## 🚀 Key Accomplishments

### 1. Modular Stories System (`src/components/CustomerStories/`)

Now, I'm fleshing out the `/api/auth/verify-email` endpoint. Both `GET` and `POST` methods will be supported for flexibility. I'm also preparing the logic for resending verification emails, along with rate limiting to prevent abuse. Plus, I need to account for Google logins, which are designed to bypass the email verification step. This requires adding a login guard to `/api/auth/login` to redirect unverified users, except for those authenticated via Google.

"# Walkthrough: Project Restructuring & Email Verification System

We have successfully promoted the codebase directly to the active IDE workspace root `C:\Users\ravil\.gemini\antigravity-ide\scratch\` and built a production-ready secure email verification system!

## 🚀 Key Accomplishments

### 1. Codebase Consolidation & Directory Promotion
Promoted all React client-side assets and Node.js server scripts from the nested `github-clone-react/` directory to the root scratch folder:
- Relocated folders: `src/`, `public/`, `backend/`.
- Relocated configurations: `.env`, `package.json`, `vite.config.js`, `tailwind.config.js`, `postcss.config.js`, `index.html`.
- Deleted the legacy nested `github-clone-react/` directory.
- Re-installed packages directly at the workspace root.

### 2. Extended Database Models (`backend/models/User.js`)
Added properties to store secure credentials and verification hashes:
- `password`: String (for email authentication).
- `verificationToken`: String (SHA256 hashed).
- `verificationTokenExpiry`: Date.
- `isVerified`: Boolean (defaults to `false` for email registrations).
- `lastLogin`: Date.

### 3. Production Verification API & NodeMailer Integration
- **Secure Token Generation**: Generates 32-byte cryptographically secure random verification tokens, storing their SHA256 hashes in MongoDB with a 30-minute expiration.
- **NodeMailer Integration**: Configured to look for SMTP credentials (`SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_USER`, `SMTP_PASS`) or fall back to a developer Ethereal SMTP account. Prints the verification links directly to the terminal console during local testing.
- **Verification Trigger (`/api/auth/verify-email`)**: Resolves incoming raw tokens, matches their hashes, activates user accounts, and deletes token metadata.
- **Login Restrictions (`/api/auth/login`)**: Block unverified logins, returning a 403 Forbidden status with a descriptive message.
- **Google OAuth bypass (`/api/auth/google`)**: Automatically registers Google accounts as pre-verified.

"# Implementation Plan: GitHub-Style User Profile & Database System

Build a high-fidelity, modular profile dashboard similar to GitHub's visual layout. This includes adding backend collections for Repositories, Contributions, and Activities, creating secure CRUD endpoints, and designing a multi-tab client profile system with a 365-day contribution calendar, statistics trackers, and repo search/filtering.

│       ├── ContributionGraph.jsx   # 365-day calendar grid & commit count details
│       ├── ActivitySection.jsx     # Commits, updates, and repo events logs
│       ├── StatsSection.jsx        # Statistics counters with hover glow
│       └── Profile.css             # Page specific style animations
│
backend/
├── models/
│   ├── Repository.js               # [NEW] Repo schema definition
│   ├── Contribution.js             # [NEW] Commit calendar logs
│   └── Activity.js                 # [NEW] Feed activities schema
└── routes/
    └── profileRoutes.js            # [NEW] CRUD handlers for repositories and profile detail updates
```

"# Walkthrough: GitHub-Style User Profile Page

We have successfully created a modular GitHub-style user profile system complete with database models, CRUD API routes, dynamic widgets, and fully-responsive layout tabs.

## 🚀 Key Accomplishments

### 1. Database Collections (`backend/models/`)
scaffolded Mongoose schemas for detailed metadata storage:
- **`Repository.js`**: Fields include `repoName`, `description`, `visibility` (public/private), `language`, `stars`, `forks`, `isPinned`, and `isArchived`.
- **`Contribution.js`**: Records daily commits mapping a compound unique index on `{ uid, date }` to track intensity metrics.
- **`Activity.js`**: Holds timeline logs of events (`commit`, `repo_created`, `starred`, `profile_update`).

### 2. REST Endpoints (`backend/routes/profileRoutes.js`)
- `GET /api/profile/:username`: Compiles user profiles, repositories owned, daily contribution calendar stats, and activity feeds.
- `PUT /api/profile/update`: Modifies bio, company, location, website URLs, skills lists, and social handles, automatically logging a `profile_update` activity.
- `POST /api/profile/repos/create`: Registers new repositories in MongoDB under a unique ID.
- `POST /api/profile/repos/pin`: Toggles pinning state for overview display.
- `POST /api/profile/repos/star`: Increments star ratings and logs stargazer feeds.
- `POST /api/profile/repos/commit`: Increases the current day's commit counter and records a commit message.

### 3. Modular React Structure (`src/pages/Profile/`)
We modularized the profile layout as requested:
- **[Profile.jsx](file:///C:/Users/ravil/.gemini/antigravity-ide/scratch/src/pages/Profile/Profile.jsx)**: Main orchestration component handling API state queries and navigation.
- **[ProfileHeader.jsx](file:///C:/Users/ravil/.gemini/antigravity-ide/scratch/src/pages/Profile/ProfileHeader.jsx)**: Implements the horizontal GitHub tabs bar (Overview, Repositories, Statistics, Activity) with slide-in underlines.

"# Walkthrough: Unified Repository & Profile Modules Synchronization

We have synchronized the repositories module with the profile page. Both pages now query the same database source and maintain a single source of truth in Redux.

## 🚀 Key Accomplishments

### 1. Single Source of Truth
- Created `setRepositories`, `updateRepository`, and `deleteRepository` reducers in `repoSlice.js`.
- Hydrates the Redux store with the database repositories whenever the profile page mounts or refreshes.
- Both `/profile` and `/repositories` query the same backend database endpoints and populate the shared Redux state instead of keeping independent copy lists.

### 2. Live Synchronization CRUD Operations
- **Create**: Posting `newRepo` to `/api/profile/repos/create` registers it in MongoDB. The new item is appended to Redux, immediately updating the project count badge and overview lists without page reloads.
- **Star & Pin**: API triggers toggle the stars/pins count on MongoDB and update Redux dynamically.
- **Rename & Edit**: Users can change the title, description, language, and visibility parameters.
- **Delete**: Users can permanently remove repositories. It decreases project counts, removes the repo card, and cleans up database entries instantly.

### 3. Component Reusability
- We isolated the search input, filtering parameters, sort order selectors, creation, and edit/delete modal frames into a shared, highly-visual `<RepositorySection>` component.
- Mounted the same `<RepositorySection>` inside both `src/pages/Profile/Profile.jsx` (under the repositories tab) and `src/pages/Repositories.jsx` to guarantee consistent aesthetics and interaction behavior.
- Link-clicks on cards from both pages open the exact same details view routes (`/repo/:repoId`).

"# Walkthrough: Profile Loading Timeout Fixes

We have resolved the `users.findOne() buffering timed out` error by disabling Mongoose command buffering globally, implementing split parallel REST endpoints, and introducing an in-memory offline database recovery fallback.

## 🚀 Key Accomplishments

### 1. Fail-Fast Database Connections (`backend/config/db.js`)
- Configured Mongoose globally to disable command buffering: `mongoose.set('bufferCommands', false)`.
- Set a database selection timeout of 3000ms (`serverSelectionTimeoutMS: 3000`) so that the backend server throws immediately when MongoDB is offline instead of hanging on buffered queries.
- Wrapped Express server startup hooks (`backend/server.js`) inside an async initialization bootstrap, waiting for database connect queries before starting port listeners.

### 2. In-Memory Offline DB Fallback Recovery
- Integrated a fail-safe offline checker inside `backend/routes/profileRoutes.js` checking `mongoose.connection.readyState === 1`.
- If MongoDB is offline, operations instantly read and write to local mock memory lists (`mockUsers`, `mockRepositories`, `mockContributions`, `mockActivities`) instead of timing out, allowing full development functionalities.

### 3. Parallel REST Endpoints & Client Loaders
- Split the monolithic profile fetch query into individual parallel requests:
  - User Details: `GET /api/profile/:username`

  - Statistics: `GET /api/profile/:username/stats`
  - Contributions: `GET /api/profile/:username/contributions`
  - Activity Feed: `GET /api/profile/:username/activity`
- Refactored `src/pages/Profile/Profile.jsx` to load sections independently in parallel, displaying skeleton placeholders on the affected area only. Users see quick user bio sidebars even if statistics or contribution calendars are slow or failing.

### 1. Database Models & Backend API Routes (`backend/`)
- **Mongoose Models**:

We have resolved the `"Not authorized, login session token is missing"` error by updating both client-side request interceptors and backend auth middleware token extraction rules.

## 🚀 Key Fixes Implemented

### 1. Multi-Source Token Extraction (`backend/middleware/authMiddleware.js`)

### 3. Redux & Context Session Persistence (`src/context/AuthContext.jsx` & `src/redux/slices/authSlice.js`)
- Updated `updateUserState` to store JWT session tokens in `localStorage` upon login/registration.

    Sidebar --> ReposList[SidebarRepositoryList]
    
    ReposList --> Redux[Redux repoSlice]
    ReposList --> Search[In-memory Search Filter]
    ReposList --> ShowMore[Show More Expansion]
    
    subgraph Navigation Routes

        Sidebar --> Issues["/issues (All Issues)"]
        Sidebar --> PRs["/pull-requests (All Pull Requests)"]

        Sidebar --> Explore["/explore (Explore)"]
        Sidebar --> Market["/marketplace (Marketplace)"]
